context:
The cleanest path is a single registry lookup in the pipeline.
Pipeline reads summary.benchmark, looks up the metric config, attaches
it to the emitted BenchmarkSummary. The frontend is purely declarative
from that point - no family logic in TypeScript.

Registry entries are strings keyed on canonical benchmark family names
(tpch, tpcds, star_schema, clickbench, nyctaxi, tsbs-devops, h2odb,
datavault, ...). Unknown families fall back to geomean_ms asc.
description:
The strategy review (2026-04-15) identified that defaulting to geometric
mean as the single ranking metric across all benchmarks is wrong:

- TPC-H and TPC-DS define **power_score** (= 3600 / geomean × scale
  adjustment) as the standard metric. Users arriving from published
  TPC results expect to see that number.
- ClickBench and SSB have no published aggregate; geomean is a
  reasonable default there.
- Custom or ad-hoc benchmarks should expose both so users can pick.

This TODO introduces a per-benchmark-family ranking metric registry and
threads it through the pipeline and UI. The matrix leaderboard uses
`power_score` for TPC-H/TPC-DS and `geomean_ms` for everything else;
both are shown in each row, but the primary sort is the canonical one.

Scope excludes computing power_score (the CLI already does this) - this
TODO only ensures the explorer surfaces and ranks by the right metric.

anti_patterns.dont: drop the secondary metric from the UI
anti_patterns.instead: show both, primary prominent, secondary muted
anti_patterns.why: some users will want to cross-reference

anti_patterns.dont: hard-code the benchmark → metric mapping in TypeScript
anti_patterns.instead: serialize the choice into the summary artifact
anti_patterns.why: it creates two sources of truth

anti_patterns.instead: read the pre-computed value and null if absent
anti_patterns.why: the CLI already emits it per-bundle

preserves.behavior: CLI-computed power_score values - do not recompute in the pipeline; read from bundle metadata
Existing `geomean_ms` field on platform rows - remains present as secondary metric for all benchmarks
The 'Canonical Duration Metric' decision from 2026-04-14 - refines, does not overturn

verifications.description: tpch artifact declares power_score as primary metric

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c 'import gzip, json; d = json.loads(gzip.open("results-explorer/public/data/benchmarks/star_schema_sf0.01_power.json.gz").read()); assert d["ranking"]["primary_metric"] == "geomean_ms"'
verifications.description: star_schema artifact declares geomean_ms as primary metric

work_units.notes:
Map benchmark family → {primary: str, secondary: str, primary_order:
'asc'|'desc'}. Initial entries:
  - tpch → power_score (desc)
  - tpcds → power_score (desc)
  - star_schema → geomean_ms (asc)
  - clickbench → geomean_ms (asc)
Fallback for unknown families: geomean_ms (asc).

Shape: {primary_metric, secondary_metric, primary_order}. Lives
alongside platform rows so the frontend does not need to know the
registry.
work_units.summary: Extend BenchmarkSummary serialization with a top-level `ranking` field

work_units.notes:
Display primary metric in a dedicated column with its unit;
display secondary metric below it in muted text. Power score has
no unit suffix (composite); geomean is "Xms". Column header is
dynamic: "Power Score" vs "Geomean" vs family-specific label.
work_units.summary: In QueryHeatmap.tsx, read summary.ranking and sort/display by primary_metric
Cross-reference RANKING_METRIC_BY_FAMILY in the strategy doc's 'Canonical Duration Metric' section
